title: Practice the work
text: How do you prepare for a job you have never done? LearnSprint lets you practice a fictional first shift in operations, where your decisions change the plan.

title: Three orders. Shared constraints.
text: Three orders share limited stock and delivery departures. I ask the warehouse what is available. The reply points to scenario facts, so I can distinguish confirmed stock from an expected arrival.

title: Make a plan, then review it
text: I allocate the kits and review the whole board. The application checks inventory over time, carrier capacity, order quantities, deadlines, and shipping cost. I decide when to record this plan.

title: The facts change
text: Then the supplier is delayed. The earlier review stays in the record, but it no longer describes the current facts. I need to respond to the changed situation.

title: An offer is not yet an agreement
text: Customer B can accept a split delivery. Asking reveals the offer; I must explicitly record the agreement before it changes the constraints. I move twenty kits to tomorrow and review the recovery plan.

title: Leave an inspectable handoff
text: The handoff preserves my plan, its assumptions, and unresolved issues. This is evidence of decisions inside a simulation, not a claim that parcels were delivered or that I am ready for a job.

title: Try a changed situation
text: A linked replay changes the opening stock and customer terms. It starts with a clean board and keeps its own help history. The report compares the saved decisions, rather than treating a repeated answer as proof of learning.

title: AI proposes. The learner decides.
text: Amazon Bedrock Nova Two Lite interprets a typed request into one bounded allocation proposal. I see the exact edit, choose Apply, and can Undo. The application still owns the facts and checks.

title: LearnSprint
text: This Alexa Plus style web simulation runs on AWS. Browser voice remains a prototype. Next comes practitioner review and a learner pilot. LearnSprint: practice the work before the first job.
